I'm willing to approve this contribution despite it being eerily similar to the 3 clashes that I will link below. First, I would like to make a suggestion: include palindromes where the letter-case differs between the first and second half (eg. kAyaK). Not necessary, I just think it's less trivial.

The similar clashes seem to differ enough, plus I think this one is the best of the lot of for reverse, but it was close.
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/70008c804cfc7fd09860ec563133116af15ba
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/103668efceb074a6eff1718c9e76726fa5c89c
https://www.codingame.com/contribute/view/1398691f8641b4c9c4df3ffa5b61ee02fc10e9

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: Palindrome is a simple question for beginners. Even though there is already a question that asks about palindromes, adding a little twist to return only palindrome words based on the user's input is still suitable for beginners. It can be solved with a bit of modification from the normal palindrome approach.

✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: The statement is clear, test cases are OK and it's solvable with basically one loop and one condition. I think this would be fun in Reverse Mode too, but, anyways, looks good to me.

It's simple and fun.

I think this is perfect for Reverse Mode as well because it's possible to notice the pattern within 5 minutes.
I hope you received enough feedback from the community to improve your contribution. Once you have made the necessary updates, publish your contribution!
Does this include palindromes with an even number of letters?
For the example, its better if the output is YES

Binary output issue
* According to the contribution guidelines, binary outputs should be avoided for clashes. That's exactly the issue with your clash, as it allows only two possible answers (either "YES" or "NO"). Please modify the output requirement to allow for more than two possible answers.

General
* There are already many clashes built around the palindrome theme. It'd be better to either develop a more original concept within that theme or consider using a different theme altogether.

Thanks.
Do you find this more useful now?
Yes but that doesn't change the code.
I agree. I think this is good for Reverse.

You seem to be a far better programmer than I but, just in case you don't know, I would like to share with you three cool tricks to enhance the solution:
[1,2,3][::-1] -> [3,2,1]
[1,2,3]  += [4] -> [1,2,3,4]
print(*[1,2,3] or [None])

Cases
